Above a critical temperature, Tc, the specific LC50 increases exponentially. Tc is considerably lower with cold‐adapted than with warm‐adapted species. The values of oxygen tolerance determined demonstrate that restriction of a species to running water is not determined by oxygen level, temperature and water flow only.

snippets.title: Effect of Dissolved Oxygen on the Survival and Hatching of Eggs of Scale Carp
snippets.label: neutral
snippets.text: Abstract Eggs of scale carp (Cyprinus carpio communis) were exposed to various levels of dissolved oxygen (DO) from fertilization to completion of hatching. Survival and hatching rate increased directly with increasing concentration of DO. Dissolved oxygen levels below 6.0 mg/1 appeared inadequate for proper survival. The retarding effect of reduced DO levels was less pronounced at early than at later stages of development.
